subject: Request: Temporary GPU pool reservation & autoscale exemption for Skyline pilot
messages:
From: Alex Moran <alex.moran@skyline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@skyline.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick heads-up: 2-week surge pilot starting Nov 10 — capacity ask

Hi Ben,

We confirmed an accelerated pilot window with our internal ML team — they want to run a 2-week throughput-focused experiment starting Nov 10 that will need sustained GPU capacity. Can Redwood support a temporary dedicated pool (NVIDIA A100 or similar) and an autoscale lock so the pool does not shrink below the reserved capacity during the test?

I attached a short plan showing expected qps and token volumes. Procurement will follow up on standard SOW/PO language.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Moran
Head of ML Platforms, Skyline AI
Skyline_Surge_MA_Plan.xlsx (attachment, 42KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Quick heads-up: 2-week surge pilot starting Nov 10 — capacity ask

Team — forwarding Skyline's ask. TL;DR: 2-week pilot, predictable sustained throughput, wants dedicated pool + autoscale floor (no shrink) Nov 10–Nov 24. Skyline is close to signing; this is a critical pilot that likely converts to a Dedicated customer.

Asks:
- Laura: can SE scope a minimal pool (gpus and expected slots) and confirm compatibility with the models they plan to run?
- Dev: can infra accommodate an autoscale exemption (prevent scale-down below X GPUs) for a short window? Any constraints or risk?
- Karthik: will this require a product rollback or special rollout policy? We may need a temporary exemption from the default autoscaler.

I attached the capacity request form they filled.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
capacity-request-form.pdf (attachment, 12KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 12:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick heads-up: 2-week surge pilot starting Nov 10 — capacity ask

Ben / team — I reviewed Skyline's plan. Early notes:

- Model mix: looks like two variants (open-llm-13b and a trimmed 7b optimized for throughput). Both are supported on our pool; we'll serve the 13b on mixed-precision profiles.
- Suggested baseline: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs with KV-cache warming and prefix caching enabled. That should sustain their peak without introducing latency spikes.
- Autoscale floor: recommend floor = 6 GPUs; autoscale can burst to 12 during peak but must not go below 6 while they're running tests.

Open questions for infra: can we implement a short-lived autoscale policy override (Nov 10–24) tied to the Skyline customer tag, and ensure billing/usage attribution remains accurate? Also confirm GPU assignment affinity so their models land on the dedicated pool.

I can share a one-pager with expected costs and latency numbers by EOD.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick heads-up: 2-week surge pilot starting Nov 10 — capacity ask

Laura — short answer: probably yes, but with caveats.

- We can create a tagged dedicated pool and pin their workloads to it, but our current autoscaler is policy-driven and shared across pools. Implementing a time-bound hard floor requires either: 1) a temporary override in the autoscale controller (manual/ops action) or 2) a sandboxed policy specific to the pool that our control plane honors. Option 2 is safer but takes ~2 workdays to QA and deploy.
- Risk: if other customers spike and nodes are exhausted region-wide, enforcing a floor increases preemption risk (we'd have to prioritize Skyline's VMs). We should document the SLA exception.
- Operational ask: need a JIRA ticket (INF-4312) for the override, and an ops runbook for rollback. We'll also need the procurement/SOW to include a clause that reserves capacity and clarifies billing for idle-backed capacity.

If we agree on floor=6 and a controlled override, I can schedule the deployment into staging Thursday and production Friday (assuming sign-off).

—Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick heads-up: 2-week surge pilot starting Nov 10 — capacity ask

Thanks for the quick triage. A few product / roadmap points:

- Policy model: product will accept a time-bound autoscale-exemption as an "SLA exception" feature we can flip per-customer (feature flag + billing tag). We should avoid harcoding per-customer config in the autoscaler.
- Backfill/priority: engineering must ensure that enforced floors do not silently starve other Dedicated customers. Suggest we add a priority weight to the scheduling decision for the pool and surface automatic alerts if cluster contended > 75%.
- Telemetry: we need a telemetry hook to capture when an exemption is active. Tie it to Optimize so we can show cost delta per token for the experiment.

Decision: approve the temporary exemption for Skyline (Nov 10–24) with floor=6 GPUs, ops runbook and JIRA ticket required before Nov 9 EOD. Finance should be copied on the billing terms in the SOW.

Ben — please confirm Skyline agrees to the floor and the billing language (idle-backed reservation). Once you confirm, Laura/Dev, please proceed with the prep plan.

—Karthik
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moran <alex.moran@skyline.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@skyline.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick heads-up: 2-week surge pilot starting Nov 10 — capacity ask

Alex — great news: product has approved a time-boxed autoscale exemption. High level:

- Reserved baseline: 6 GPUs minimum in a Skyline-dedicated pool; burst to 12 available.
- Window: Nov 10 00:00 UTC — Nov 24 23:59 UTC (we agreed to UTC window for clarity).
- Billing: idle-backed reservation billing applies for the floor; procurement — please confirm PO language so finance can finalize charges.
- Next steps: Laura will send the one-pager with latency/cost figures; Dev will open INF-4312 and deliver the ops runbook. Both must be complete by Nov 9 EOD.

Can you confirm acceptance of the above and share the signed SOW/PO when available?

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
